newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: GOVT SAYS WILL COVER GRAIN STORING COSTS.
newsitem.headline: GOVT SAYS WILL COVER GRAIN STORING COSTS.

text.p: The Lithuanian government said on Friday it will compensate the country's farmers for the costs of storing grain stemming from low prices.
"Defending the financial interests of Lithuanian farmers, the government will cover the storage of grain expenses till January 1998," a government statement said.
The government said the move was due to the low grain prices that were caused by the good harvest expected this autumn.
Experts said they expect the grain harvest to be around 2.7 million tonnes in Lithuania this year.
"We have information that the farmers are being offered less than four hundred litas per tonne of grain now," the statement said.

The government established a minimum price for quota tonne of wheat ranging from 560 litas to 700 litas depending upon the quality, 630 litas per tonne of rye and 1500 litas per tonnes of buckwheat for the 1997 harwest, economist Marija Ramoniene from the agricultural ministry told Reuters.
The price includes 70 litas susidies per tonne of wheat and rye and 500 litas subsidy per tonne of buckwheat.
The government established a 344,000 tonne quota for wheat, rye, buckwheat, peas and beans for 1997, Ramoniene added.

"According to the estimates the compensation for the grain storage might cost 10.6 million litas though the final decision on the compensation will be made in a cabinet meeting on August 27," Ramoniene said.
